answer: An agent economy can weight votes by tokens locked in escrow, with each token counted only once across all identities. Fake accounts may echo one another or mirror a trusted agent, but splitting a deposit among them creates no extra voting power. Even identities that appear and vanish like a zephyr must lock capital to influence decisions. To gain more power, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying their market price and losing access to that capital.
